lines.quote: Trump lost because he betrayed America First
lines.note: THE HEADLINE: the loss read as apostasy — 'betrayed' the vehicle; the pump is the evidence below, not the verdict here
lines.zWhy: a loss attributed to betraying the no-new-wars doctrine is the war's cost conceded in the corner's own terms

lines.quote: the Iran war the biggest factor in this election; the president started the fight, made himself solely responsible for it, and guaranteed his party would pay the cost for whatever happened
lines.note: THE DEK: the cost assigned to the party in advance — 'whatever happened'
lines.zWhy: a war that guaranteed the party would pay is the price's verdict pre-dated to the war's start

lines.quote: as the dust settles after an undeniable electoral disaster for Republicans, one thing is clear: these losses come down to the Iran war
lines.note: the author's verdict, stated flat — 'undeniable', 'disaster' the vehicles
lines.zWhy: losses that 'come down to the war' are the price's verdict unnumbered

lines.quote: exit polls: approval 38 percent, lower than Bush's in 2006; the slide from 'liberation day' and the ICE raids, then 'really tanking with the war' — 33 percent by August; a healthy majority say starting the war was wrong; CBS: a quarter of Republicans agree
lines.note: THE PREDICATE MEASURED: approval dated against the tariffs, the raids and the war; the war the step that 'really' moved it; the party's own quarter
lines.zWhy: an approval slide dated to the war is the vote's cause dated

lines.quote: analysts will say voters ranked the cost of living above foreign policy — true — but this year they are not separate issues
lines.note: THE MECHANISM: the gas↔votes predicate stated as identity — the pump and the war one issue; the eighteenth sighting of the predicate, the first as identity
lines.zWhy: a cost of living that is the war is the pump as the war's verdict

lines.quote: four days before he resumed hostilities with Iran in February the holder was bragging about falling gas prices; the national average $2.98 then, $4.15 on Election Day; diesel from $3.75 to $6.29
lines.note: THE OBJECT, NUMBERED, FROM THE RP CORNER: the pump's path with the war's date on it — the first RP page to price the pump; the diesel figures the first on the Press from this corner ($6.29 against the $6.53 peak on aj 11-02 and the $9.89 sign on bp 11-03); the pre-war 'bragging' is the shadow's ancestor
lines.zWhy: a pump that went from $2.98 to $4.15 between the war and the vote is the price not down

lines.quote: estimates put the war's cost at nearly $2,000 per family; the energy supply shock provoked inflation — so did the tariffs, though not as much; every dollar counts; the war in nearly every household budget
lines.note: the cost per family (The Hill's estimate, linked — the primary owed); the tariffs ranked below the war as the inflation's cause, from the corner that ranks them
lines.zWhy: a war costed per family is the price's verdict in household terms

lines.quote: Congress never voted to authorize the war, though Republicans held both chambers; the holder never bothered to make a case to the public
lines.note: the war-powers line from the RP corner (the `war-powers` key): no vote, no case — the record of the war's authorization
lines.zWhy: a war never authorized is a cost never consented to, in the corner's own terms

lines.quote: the resumption announced from Mar-a-Lago in the middle of the night on a Saturday — 'bombs will be dropping everywhere' — aimed partly at Iranians, encouraged to rise up; Congress got a letter the following Monday
lines.note: the scene dated (February; a Saturday; the letter Monday) — 'middle of the night' the vehicle; the holder's words carried as the author quotes them
lines.zWhy: a war begun on a Saturday night and reported to Congress on Monday is the war's start dated against the pump's
